record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Quantum violation of every proper Bell inequality
record.original_question: In the same no-signalling, quantum, and classical correlation setting, let a proper Bell inequality be a maximal-face inequality of the classical local polytope C that is not also a face of the no-signalling polytope P, so it is not implied merely by positivity and no-signalling. Can every such proper Bell inequality be violated by some quantum correlation data, meaning that Q has points outside the corresponding classical face?

evidence.quote:
Problem 26.B:
Consider a maximal face of the polytope C, which is not also a face of P (a blue line in the above figure). In other words, consider a ”proper Bell inequality”, i. e., a tight linear inequality for local classical correlations, which does not follow from positivity and no-signalling.
Then can we find points of Q outside the face? Or, phrased in terms of Bell inequalites, can every proper Bell inequality be violated by quantum correlation data?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a bipartite Bell scenario with two parties (Alice and Bob), each choosing one of finitely many measurement settings and obtaining one of finitely many outcomes. A behavior is a family of joint conditional probability distributions p(a,b | x,y), where x, y are the measurement choices and a, b are the outcomes. Inside the simplex of all such families, define:

- P: the no-signalling polytope, consisting of all behaviors satisfying nonnegativity, normalization, and the no-signalling constraints (the marginal of a given x is independent of y, and vice versa).
- C ⊆ P: the classical (local) polytope, the convex hull of all deterministic local behaviors p(a,b|x,y) = δ_{a,f(x)} δ_{b,g(y)} for functions f, g.
- Q with C ⊆ Q ⊆ P: the set of quantum behaviors, those of the form p(a,b|x,y) = Tr[(E^x_a ⊗ F^y_b) ρ] for some density operator ρ on a tensor-product Hilbert space and POVMs {E^x_a}_a, {F^y_b}_b.

Call a linear inequality on behaviors a proper Bell inequality if it defines a maximal (facet) face of C that is not also a face of P; equivalently, it is a tight inequality for the local set that does not follow from positivity and no-signalling alone.

Question: Is it true that for every proper Bell inequality, there exists a quantum behavior in Q that violates it? Equivalently, does Q contain points strictly outside every facet of C that is not a facet of P?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to still be open in full generality. Partial results are known: all tight correlation Bell inequalities in the two-party binary-outcome setting have quantum violations (Phys. Rev. Research 2, 012044), and all two-party facet Bell inequalities are violated by almost-quantum correlations (Phys. Rev. Research 3, 033100; arXiv:2004.07673). The general statement for arbitrary multipartite/multi-outcome scenarios with the actual quantum set Q is not established, and the question is listed among open quantum problems.

status_evidence.title: All tight correlation Bell inequalities have quantum violations
status_evidence.snippet: Tight Bell inequalities always have a quantum violation for any bipartite setting of binary measurements.
status_evidence.claim: Resolves the question affirmatively in the two-party binary-outcome correlation setting.

status_evidence.title: Violation of all two-party facet Bell inequalities by almost-quantum correlations
status_evidence.snippet: Every tight Bell inequality is violated by almost-quantum correlations, an SDP relaxation of the quantum set.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result using the almost-quantum (not exactly quantum) set.

status_evidence.title: Bell inequalities holding for all quantum states – Open Quantum Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems regarding Bell inequalities and quantum violations.
status_evidence.claim: Listed among open quantum problems, indicating the general question remains open.
